title.es: Would rather, it's time y preferencias

objective: Al terminar expresas preferencias, consejos y urgencia con 'It's (about) time', 'would rather', 'had better' y 'as if / as though' + pasado.

warmup.prompt_es: El inglés usa el pasado para hablar del presente en ciertas estructuras: 'It's time we left', 'I'd rather you stayed'. Aprendes estas estructuras para dar consejos y expresar preferencias con precisión.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: It's about time we made a decision. The trip is in three weeks.
lines.es: Ya es hora de que tomemos una decisión. El viaje es en tres semanas.

lines.speaker: Eva
lines.text: I'd rather we went to the mountains than to the beach.
lines.es: Yo preferiría que fuéramos a la montaña antes que a la playa.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Really? I'd rather you didn't suggest the mountains. Last time you behaved as if you were an expert, and we nearly got lost.
lines.es: ¿En serio? Preferiría que no propusieras la montaña. La última vez te comportaste como si fueras una experta y casi nos perdemos.

lines.speaker: Eva
lines.text: That's unfair! I'd rather stay at home than argue about it.
lines.es: ¡Eso no es justo! Prefiero quedarme en casa antes que discutir por eso.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Sorry. You'd better forgive me, or we'll never agree on anything.
lines.es: Perdona. Más te vale perdonarme, o no nos pondremos de acuerdo nunca.

lines.speaker: Eva
lines.text: All right. Suppose we compromise: two days in the mountains and three at the coast.
lines.es: Vale. Supongamos que cedemos: dos días en la montaña y tres en la costa.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Perfect. It's high time we booked the hotels. I'd rather you did it, if you don't mind.
lines.es: Perfecto. Ya es hora más que sobrada de reservar los hoteles. Preferiría que lo hicieras tú, si no te importa.

lines.speaker: Eva
lines.text: Fine, but you'd better pay for the first night!
lines.es: Vale, ¡pero más te vale pagar la primera noche!

glossary.es: ya es hora más que sobrada

md_es: **Estructuras que usan el pasado para el presente o futuro**
| Estructura | Significado | Ejemplo |
| **It's (about / high) time + sujeto + pasado** | ya es hora de que… | *It's time we left.* |
| **It's time + to + verbo** | es hora de | *It's time to leave.* |
| **I'd rather + base** (mismo sujeto) | preferiría | *I'd rather stay at home.* |
| **I'd rather + sujeto + pasado** (sujeto distinto) | preferiría que | *I'd rather you stayed.* |
| **I'd rather have + participio** | me hubiera gustado más | *I'd rather have stayed.* |
| **had better + base** | más vale que | *You'd better go now.* |
| **as if / as though + pasado** | como si | *He talks as if he knew everything.* |
| **suppose / supposing + presente o pasado** | supongamos que | *Suppose we compromise.* |
**It's time**
- *It's time to go.* (infinitivo, sin sujeto distinto) · *It's time we went.* (con sujeto, pasado con valor de presente).
- *It's high time you stopped smoking.* (reproche suave).
**Would rather**
- Mismo sujeto: *I'd rather walk than take the bus.* (sin *to*).
- Distinto sujeto: *I'd rather you didn't smoke here.* (pasado simple, valor presente/futuro).
- Pasado: *I'd rather you hadn't told her.* (pasado perfecto).
- Negativo: *I'd rather not go.* · *I'd rather not.*
- Comparación: *I'd rather walk than drive.* (*than* + base) · *prefer walking to driving.*
**Had better**
- *You'd better tell him.* Forma negativa: *You'd better not be late.* (sin *to*). Se usa para advertencias o consejos fuertes.
**As if / as though**
- Situación irreal: *He behaves as if he were the boss.* (subjuntivo con *were*, también *was*).
- Situación probable: *It looks as if it's going to rain.* (presente).
- Pasado: *She looked as if she had seen a ghost.*
**Errores típicos**
- ✘ *It's time we go to bed.* → ✔ *It's time we went to bed.* / *It's time to go to bed.*
- ✘ *I'd rather to stay at home.* → ✔ *I'd rather stay at home.*
- ✘ *I'd rather you don't smoke.* → ✔ *I'd rather you didn't smoke.*
- ✘ *You had better to go.* → ✔ *You had better go. / You'd better go.*
- ✘ *He talks as if he is rich* (si no lo es) → ✔ *as if he were rich.*
**Ojo:** *I'd* puede ser *I would* (rather) o *I had* (better). *You'd better* = *you had better*. En negativo: *had better not*.
Pronunciación: *rather* /ˈrɑːðə/ · *compromise* /ˈkɒmprəmaɪz/ · *behave* /bɪˈheɪv/.
